characters.name: Lydia Tár
characters.description: A world-renowned classical conductor and composer whose brilliance is undermined by growing anxieties, betrayals, and the weight of her own ambition.

characters.name: Francesca Lentini
characters.description: Lydia’s loyal assistant—efficient, young, and perceptive—who balances reverence for her mentor with growing unease at Lydia’s extremes.

characters.name: Adam Gopnik
characters.description: A thoughtful New Yorker writer who conducts the on-stage interview, offering Lydia both praise and pointed questions.

characters.name: Eliot Kaplan
characters.description: A well-connected patron whose mix of flattery and self-interest tests Lydia’s patience and integrity.

characters.name: Sharon Goodnow
characters.description: Lydia’s partner and fellow musician, whose calm support masks her own worries about family and Lydia’s unraveling.

characters.name: Petra
characters.description: Lydia and Sharon’s six-year-old adopted daughter, caught between her parents’ brilliance and their growing tensions.

characters.name: Max
characters.description: A young Juilliard conductor student whose idealism is challenged by Lydia’s uncompromising standards.

characters.name: Olive Kerr
characters.description: A conducting student chosen for critique, representing the next generation of musicians grappling with artistic intent.

characters.name: Sebastian Brix
characters.description: Lydia’s longtime assistant conductor whose traditionalist approach both comforts and frustrates her.

characters.name: Andris Davis
characters.description: Lydia’s venerable predecessor in Berlin—a mentor-figure whose praise once shaped her career.

characters.name: Johanna
characters.description: Petra’s schoolmate whose bullying provokes Lydia’s fierce, protective side.
